question: In relation to clopidogrel, it is false that:

options.opa: It is structurally related to thienopyridines.
options.opb: It inhibits adenyl cyclase, and therefore increases cAMP levels.
options.opc: It has a low index of myelotoxicity in relation to ticlopidine.
options.opd: It has a longer action in relation to ticlopidine.
options.ope: In case of surgical intervention, it is recommended to interrupt the treatment at least one week in advance.

analysis: Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medication that is structurally related to thienopyridines and works by inhibiting the P2Y12 component of ADP receptors on the platelet surface, which prevents activation of the GPIIb/IIIa receptor complex, thereby reducing platelet aggregation. It does not inhibit adenyl cyclase or increase cAMP levels; this mechanism is more associated with drugs like dipyridamole. Clopidogrel is known to have a lower risk of myelotoxicity compared to ticlopidine and generally has a longer duration of action. It is recommended to discontinue clopidogrel at least 5-7 days before surgery to reduce the risk of bleeding.
